h1: A Local Something — a shophouse hostel in central Trang with a hidden 5th-floor rooftop bar
intro: If you are backpacking through Trang on a tight budget but still want somewhere with character rather than a bland dorm, A Local Something is the converted-shophouse hostel in the city centre that many reviews call the best hostel in Trang · Walls painted with bright art, well-organised dorms, a shared kitchen, and the Hidden Something rooftop bar on the 5th floor where you can sip craft beer and look out over the town all evening · It is about a 2-minute walk to Chan Chala Night Market and sits right beside Trang train station · A 2-star hostel from approx. THB 470/night for a dorm bed · Score 9.2 — this place sells design, atmosphere and location, not luxury.

body.html: The first thing that sets A Local Something apart from an ordinary hostel is that the building is an old shophouse, thoughtfully renovated · Open the door and you walk into a bright common room with light-blue walls covered in art, a long wooden table for eating or chatting with fellow travellers, and a shared kitchen to use · That atmosphere is exactly why solo travellers say it feels more like home than a hotel — it is the single thing international reviews mention most.

There are just 7 rooms, split between bunk-bed dorms and private rooms · The dorms come in mixed and female-only versions, with each bed laid out as its own little nook: a reading lamp, power outlet, clothes hanger, locker and a thick mattress with good linens · The private rooms include a double with an en-suite bathroom, ideal for travellers who want a bit more privacy while keeping the hostel vibe · Every room is air-conditioned, Wi-Fi is free, and housekeeping is daily — cleanliness scores are near-perfect across every platform.
"The best hostel in Trang. The staff are so friendly and helpful, the rooftop bar has a great view and local food, and it genuinely feels like home."

The highlight everyone talks about is the Hidden Something rooftop bar & bistro on the 5th floor · It is a small rooftop bar where you sip craft beer, eat local food, sometimes catch live acoustic music, and look out over Trang in every direction · Many reviews say the atmosphere punches well above the price — good for a solo drink, a night out with friends or a date · Because the bar is inside the hostel, you have a relaxed place to spend the evening without going anywhere, and it is where guests naturally end up meeting each other.

Location is another strong point · The hostel sits on Kantang Road in Thap Thiang, central Trang — about a 2-minute walk to Chan Chala Night Market, right beside Trang train station, with more than a dozen restaurants within easy walking distance · If you arrive in Trang by train, you can step off and wheel your bag straight in · Staff help arrange transport and boat tours to Trang's islands, there is paid airport transfer, luggage storage and laundry — it makes an easy base before heading out to the islands.

A few things to know before you book · First, because it is a small hostel, you have to accept some noise and so-so sleep in the dorms — the sleep-quality score sits a touch below the others, so light sleepers should bring earplugs or choose a private room · Second, a few reviews mention mosquitoes in the common area at times, so pack repellent · Third, some staff speak limited English, even if they are helpful overall · And it is an old shophouse with no lift, so the rooms and bar are upstairs and you will be climbing stairs.

Prices start at around THB 470/night for a dorm bed at the lower end, with private rooms climbing to roughly THB 700–1,100 depending on room type and season · Overall scores are very high: Tripadvisor gives it 4.8/5 and ranks it #7 of 30 specialty lodgings in Trang, while booking-platform reviews give near-perfect marks for cleanliness, location and atmosphere · The numbers show a small hostel that scores high in the budget bracket.

In short, A Local Something suits backpackers, solo travellers and laid-back couples who want to stay in central Trang on a budget and value atmosphere, design and meeting people · If you come to Trang for morning dim sum, market walks, an evening drink and using the city as a base to reach the islands, it fits perfectly · But if you want quiet privacy, a pool or hotel-style facilities, look instead at a city hotel like Thumrin Thana or a boutique like Namthip Residence.

A tip from reading the reviews: head up to the Hidden Something rooftop bar between sunset and evening, when the atmosphere is at its best · If you sleep lightly, choose a private room over a dorm, and book ahead because there are only 7 rooms and they fill fast in high season · Arriving by train is the easiest option since the hostel is right beside the station.

honestSummary: A Local Something is a design hostel in a central-Trang shophouse that stands out for atmosphere, cleanliness, location and its rooftop bar · 7 rooms across dorms and private rooms, prices from a few hundred baht, a short walk to the night market and right beside the train station · But accept that it is a small hostel — dorm noise and sleep are a compromise, and there are no hotel-style facilities.
honestChecks: If you sleep lightly and want privacy — dorms in a small hostel can be noisy and the sleep score sits below the others → choose a private room or bring earplugs.
If you want a pool or hotel-style facilities — this is a small shophouse hostel without them → pick a city hotel like Thumrin Thana or the Namthip Residence boutique instead.
If you want to be on the beach or near the sea — this is in the city centre, not by the water → for the coast, choose accommodation around Pak Meng, Sikao or on Trang's islands instead.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — A Local Something, Trang

faq.q: Where is A Local Something and how do I get there?
faq.a: It is at 88 Kantang Road, Thap Thiang, Mueang Trang, in central Trang · It sits right beside Trang train station and is about a 2-minute walk to Chan Chala Night Market · Trang Airport (TST) is roughly a 15-minute drive · Arriving by train is easiest — you step off and walk straight in.

faq.q: How much does A Local Something cost and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Prices start at around THB 470/night for a bed in a mixed dorm · a female-only dorm bed is about THB 520 · a private double with en-suite bathroom is about THB 700, rising to roughly THB 1,100 in high season · Prices vary by date, so always compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Who is A Local Something best for?
faq.a: It suits backpackers, solo travellers and laid-back couples who want to stay in central Trang on a budget and value atmosphere, design and meeting people · It is great for using the city as a base before heading out to the islands · It is not ideal for anyone wanting a pool or hotel-style privacy.

faq.q: Does A Local Something really have a rooftop bar?
faq.a: Yes · it is called the Hidden Something rooftop bar & bistro on the 5th floor · It serves craft beer and local food, has live acoustic music on some nights, and looks out over Trang in every direction · It is the highlight reviews mention most, best from late afternoon into the evening.

faq.q: Is A Local Something good for families or light sleepers?
faq.a: It is a small dorm-focused hostel · light sleepers should choose the private double over a dorm and bring earplugs · A few reviews mention mosquitoes in the common area at times, so pack repellent · Children aged 6+ are allowed under conditions, but the vibe suits travellers more than families with young children.

faq.q: Is it easy to reach Trang's islands from A Local Something?
faq.a: Yes — it is central and beside the train station · Staff can arrange minivans and boat tours to Koh Kradan, Koh Mook, Koh Ngai and the Emerald Cave · Most depart from Pak Meng or Kuan Tung Ku piers, about a 40–50 minute drive from the city before the boat transfer.
